topics.label: Lecture introduction and framing
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic frames the lecture by introducing complement, its significance, and its historical reputation in immunology.

topics.label: Core principles, nomenclature, and central C3 activation
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics introduce the general architecture, naming conventions, and central C3 cleavage reaction of the complement system.

topics.label: Pathways of complement activation
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics detail the alternative, lectin, and classical pathways that trigger complement activation and converge on C3 deposition.

topics.label: Effector mechanisms of complement
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain the downstream immune outcomes mediated by activated complement components, including opsonization, inflammation, and pathogen lysis.

topics.label: Complement regulation and host protection
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic explores the regulatory proteins and mechanisms that prevent complement from damaging host cells.

topics.label: Clinical consequences of complement deficiencies
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic details the diverse clinical presentations and disease phenotypes that arise from deficiencies in specific complement components.

topics.label: Pathogen evasion of complement
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic explains the evolutionary strategies pathogens deploy to circumvent complement attack, focusing on Staphylococcus aureus mechanisms.

topics.label: Lecture conclusion and preview
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic concludes the complement lecture and previews the upcoming session on the adaptive immune system.
